key_insight: AI-based tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte scoring methods, including TRIGS and SAM-TIL, can predict response and survival in triple-negative and HER2-positive breast cancer with prognostic performance similar to clinical scoring.
clinical_relevance: These tools may help standardize and scale TIL assessment in breast cancer, but they are not yet interchangeable with pathologist scoring for clinical use.
method: Updated an automated TIL pipeline to align with clinical scoring guidelines (TRIGS).
Tested foundation model-based lymphocyte detection (SAM-TIL) and compared it with HoVerNet, muTILs, and gold-standard clinical assessment.
Evaluated associations with pCR, overall survival, and event-free survival across TransNEO, TCGA, and PARTNER cohorts.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, TRIGS and SAM-TIL showed significant prediction of pCR and survival, with correlation to clinical assessment of 0.59–0.69 and similar pCR/EFS performance across methods.
watch_item: Model-generated lymphocyte scores did not match gold-standard clinical assessment closely enough to replace pathologist review, so independent validation is still needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: Tumour region identification guided scoring (TRIGS) and foundation model-based Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocyte scoring are prognostic for pathological complete response/event free survival in the triple negative patients in the PARTNER randomized controlled trial
